# Metric library

Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company.

Module id `metrics`, in [src/modules/metrics/](../../../src/modules/metrics/module.json).

## What it adds to the core

| Extension point | What |
|---|---|
| Needs | none |
| Routes | `/metrics`, `/metrics/new`, `/metrics/:metricId`, `/metrics/:metricId/edit` |
| Old addresses | `/data/metrics` → `/metrics` |
| Navigation | Metrics |
| Places on core screens | `goal.facts`, `goal.measure`, `goal.sections`, `people.person`, `people.team`, `checkin.number`, `checkin.table` |
| Drawn for it by the core while it is on | `workspace.about`, `afterGoalSaved`, `beforeCheckIn`, `onSwitch`, `drill` ([what each is](../../rebuild/module-platform.md#what-a-module-needs-that-faros-core-still-draws): Faro’s core code asks whether it is on; a rebuild builds each as a place or hook) |
| Workspace sections | none |
| Database tables | `okr_metrics` (0033_metric_library.sql): The metric library: one row per metric, never deleted (removed_at when removed).; `okr_goal_metrics` (0033_metric_library.sql): Which metric measures a goal, and for which slice (a team, or the whole company when team_id is null): one row per goal, removed_at when unlinked. |
| Its own records | metric (`okr_metrics`, filed under `modules.metrics.metrics`; removable and restorable); metric link (`okr_goal_metrics`, filed under `modules.metrics.metricLinks`) |
| AI tools | `list_metrics`, `get_metric`, `save_metric`, `remove_metric`, `retire_metric`, `merge_metrics`, `link_goal_metric`, `save_baselines`, `verify_metric` |
| Help articles | “Metrics: what each number means” (`metrics`), “Defining a metric well” (`metric-define`), “Measured by: choosing a goal’s metric” (`metric-measured-by`), “Measured by: for whom, and which part” (`metric-slices`), “Changing, retiring and merging a metric” (`metric-change`), “When a number isn’t measured yet” (`metric-measurement`), “Where a metric sits, and how far to trust it” (`metric-structure`), “Draft, Defined and Verified metrics” (`metric-quality`), “Metrics in a spreadsheet” (`metric-sheet`) |
| Outside its folder | none |

## Requirements

- `METRICS-LIBRARY`: Anyone can find a metric, read what it means, and see every goal measured by it side by side (ML1). Metrics (/metrics, in the menu after People; on a phone under More) lists every metric in use A to Z ignoring case and accents, 50 a page; a search matches the name, unit, "lower is better" or "higher is better", the owner and the meaning; filters for the unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, the owner, which way is better, no goals, and something to sort out; sorts A to Z, most goals first and changed lately; everything in the address. A row links to the metric, says its unit, direction and owner, and its goals by status as shape and word, worst first. A metric's page says what it means and how it's calculated, then its goals as a table (status, goal, for, now, target with its week, against plan, owner), worst first, with the lowest and highest now when two or more have a number, then its source, the source's owner, refresh, caveats and who added and last changed it. Its owner and admins see what it still needs and can change or remove it; everyone else sees who can. A goal's summary says what measures it; a person's page lists the metrics they own and a team's the metrics its goals use. Old addresses under /data/metrics lead to the library, a metric or the form. (Copy.)
- `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`: A goal's metric is chosen by typing to find it where the goal is made or changed, or added there, and fills in what the metric already says (ML2). In New goal, "Measured by" is the first field on the measure step (under the name when changing a goal), never for a goal with dated stages or for someone who may not link the goal: find-and-pick with "No metric" first, metrics in the goal's unit offered first, and "Add “…” as a new metric" last. Choosing one shows its meaning, the goal's team or the whole company under "For", and, on a new goal whose unit and decimals nobody typed, sets them from the metric and says so in one line with "Use different ones". A unit that differs stops the save with the reason. Added in place, a metric needs a name, a unit and which way is better, is owned by whoever adds it, and is chosen. Check says "Measured by {metric}, for {team}". Goals filters by the metric (?metric=, "Measured by" in the filter line), and a metric's page opens Goals filtered to it. (Copy.)
- `METRICS-CARE`: A metric's owner and admins are shown what it is missing; removing or changing one says what happens to its goals (ML3). A metric's page lists, for its owner and admins only, what it still needs in order (no owner, no meaning, no source, no goal after 14 days), each with a button that opens the form at that field. Adding a metric whose name is close to one in use (one name's words contain the other's, or they share two words and differ by one, leaving out filler words and brackets) asks "This looks like …" as a Check (METRIC-DEFINED), with Use that one or Mine is different: keep it. The form keeps a draft through Close, Back and a reload; each error shows under its field once the field is left or on the first try to save, and the first field in error takes the focus. Changing the unit or direction of a metric goals use asks first, saying how many goals and how many will show a warning. Remove says which goals stop being measured (a stopped goal's too); Undo puts the metric and its links back, and Put it back later restores the links it had to goals still there. Workspace → About tells admins how many metrics have no owner, with See them. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-DEFINED`: A metric can be used with a name, a unit and a direction; what it still lacks is said in words, never scored; and a likely mistake in its name, unit or meaning is questioned before it is saved (MT1). Add a metric asks for Name, Unit (with Decimal places, optional, 0 if left) and Which way is better, then what it means, then, under "Where the number comes from · can be said later", its source, who owns that source and how often it refreshes, then its owner and caveats. A Must fix shows under its field outlined and washed with the warning mark and "Must fix"; a Check under its field with the warning mark, "Check" and its answers as plain buttons; neither uses a status shape. The foot says "{a} to fix, {b} to check." and the completeness line. The Checks: a name one letter (two for names over 12 characters; never for 4 or fewer) or a word from another metric's, or one a metric used to have; a unit spelt differently from one in use; a percentage or rate whose meaning doesn't say out of what. Saving is refused while a Must fix stands, and with a Check unanswered it scrolls to it and says "Answer the question above first."; an answered Check closes to one line with Change. A metric's page says "Fully defined" or "Still to say: …" (and "Its owner has left.") under its title, for everyone, with each item a link to the form's field for its owner and admins. get_metric returns the line; save_metric returns unanswered checks without saving and takes answers. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-PARTS`: A goal is measured by a metric for a team or the whole company and optionally one part of that number, takes the metric's unit and direction, and says why when what measures it changes after check-ins (MT2). "Measured by" shows "From the metric" ({unit}, {decimals in words}, {direction}, and where the number comes from) and, under For, "Which part" (optional, at most 60 characters), with the parts other goals on the metric use offered under it. A part spelt like one in use (the same once case, accents, punctuation and a trailing s are set aside, or one edit away; never for two characters) is a Check (Use it / Keep yours); another live goal on the same metric, team and part is a Check (Carry on). On a goal with check-ins, changing its metric, For or part needs Why, which its History entry gives. A goal's About lists Measured by: For, What it means, From the metric, Where the number comes from, Caveats, This goal's own and, when it differs from the metric's meaning, For this goal. A metric's page shows each goal's For with its part. link_goal_metric takes part and reason, returns checks and saves nothing until it gets answers. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-CHANGE`: A metric that changes tells its goals (MT3). Changing a metric goals use reads back what it does to them first: a new meaning or source asks "Is it still the same number?"; "The number itself changes" and a new direction each need a reason, and leave a mark on every goal's chart ("Definition changed, week {w}", a dashed hairline labelled beside it) and History; a new unit is a new label (every goal's unit changes too) or a different scale, refused. A metric that has measured a goal is retired, not deleted: its goals keep their links and numbers and say "Measured by {metric}, retired {date}", it leaves the pickers, and Bring it back undoes it. Admins merge a metric into another in the same unit, moving its goals and retiring it pointing there. Every one of these saves with one Undo, and retire_metric, merge_metrics and save_metric's comparable, reason and relabel do the same through MCP. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-MEASUREMENT`: A gap in measurement is visible and owned, not faked (MS). Each metric says whether it is measured today, Measured, Partly or Gap, always as a shape (a filled, half-filled or broken square) and its word, with an optional line on what is missing (at most 300 characters). A metric with a gap or measured only in part is listed under To sort out on its page and in the library ("Not measured yet: {n} goals held to no number", "Only partly measured") with Say how it's measured. A goal measured by a metric with a gap is held to no number: it says Not measured yet (a broken ring and the words) instead of a status, nothing on it is due, late or quiet, and it projects nothing; linking it to a measured metric, unlinking it, or its metric being measured holds it to its plan again, in the same save, with one Undo and a line in its History. save_metric takes measurement and measurement_note, and get_metric and the export say so. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-STRUCTURE`: A metric keeps the register's structure (MQ): an optional parent metric and how it relates to it (component, driver, control or breakdown; a level needs a parent, and no metric is its own parent or under itself), a confidence in its number (high, medium or low) and how it could be gamed, in words beside its definition. Its page says where it sits and lists the metrics under it. save_metric takes parent, level, confidence and gaming, and get_metric says them. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-SHEET`: Metrics go out in the workbook and come back through the same preview, rules and undo as any import, and loading an export back changes nothing (MI, round 2's MT6). A row adds a metric (empty ID), or changes one found by ID or by name, any case; Action retires one (with a Reason) or brings one back; an absent column or an empty cell keeps what the metric says. Each refusal and question is the library's own, in the same words as the form: a name used twice, a direction or refresh it can't read, an owner who isn't here, a unit a file can't change on a metric goals use, a change of meaning on one ("Is it still the same number?"; the number changing needs a Reason), a name one letter from another. It carries the metric's structure (MQ) as Part of (another metric, by name or ID, in the library or on an earlier row), How it relates (Component, Driver, Control or Breakdown), Confidence (High, Medium or Low) and How it could be gamed, and refuses in the library's words a Part of that would put a metric under itself (a loop) and a How it relates with no Part of. The preview counts new and changed metrics, and one Undo puts every row back. bulk_change takes a metrics list with the same columns. With the Metric library off, the sheet is said once ("Metric library is off in {workspace}, so the Metrics sheet was not read.") and nothing of it is read. (Copy.) Tests: `src/modules/metrics/sheetPlan.test.ts`.
- `METRIC-STAGE`: Every metric is Draft, Defined or Verified (MQ2), worked out from what it says and shown as a step shape plus its word. Defined needs ten parts: meaning; what is measured, how it is aggregated and what each part counts (a ratio's numerator and denominator); each part's filters and exclusions; unit; direction; a structured window; the source with a link to the report or query; the source's owner; refresh; and an owner who is here. A Draft metric can measure a goal (it warns, never blocks). Verified lasts 12 months; changing the calculation, window, source or direction asks once and drops it to Defined with the reason kept; a reworded filter or exclusion asks the last verifier to confirm instead. list_metrics filters by stage and to_verify and gives each row's stage, refresh, window and what it still needs; get_metric and save_metric give the stage, save_metric before and after. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-VERIFY`: A metric is verified by anyone but its owner and whoever last changed its calculation, window or source, and then only by an admin, someone in the source's owner or a verifier an admin named. They say they opened the link and give the period, the figure they got and a note; Faro shows the difference from the figure it has (a baseline, else the latest reading), with no fixed tolerance. The outcome is Verified, or Couldn't reproduce (kept, the stage unchanged, on the owner's To sort out until answered). verify_metric does the same and refuses in words that say who can instead. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-BASELINES`: A metric keeps a baseline per slice (the company, or a team, and an optional part): value, the period it covers, the day taken and how, all required. A new one moves the old one to History; a new figure for the same period, or one changed from the figure read, needs a reason. Baselines never change the stage. A new source flags them as taken from the old source, to retake. save_baselines sets one or many, and from_readings fills last quarter's figures for confirming without saving. (Copy.) Tests: `evals/mcp.eval.ts`.
- `READING-PREFILL`: When a goal is measured by a metric that a registered number source reads for the link's own slice (its team and part), the check-in's number step asks the source once when it opens and fills the field with the latest reading: "From {source}, read {when}." (in the viewer's zone: "9:02 today", "16:40 yesterday", else "9:00 on Thu 5 Nov") and the step's primary names the number ("Confirm 12 min"). Nothing is ever posted for the owner: a week with a reading and no check-in has no check-in. A source that reads only the whole company never fills in a team's goal ("{source} measures this for the whole company, not for {team} on its own, so it isn't filled in."); no source, no number yet, nothing new since the last check-in and a source that can't be reached each say so, and the step is otherwise as without a source. With the Metric library off, the step is exactly as it was. (Copy.)
- `READING-RECORDED-ONLY`: A number typed over a reading asks "Why is it different?" with four choices (the source is behind: I have a newer number; counts something else; is wrong this week; something else, which needs at least 10 characters of Say more) before "Use {typed} {unit}". The owner's number is the check-in's; the reading (source, value, when measured) and the reason are recorded beside it, by the same rule at every door (the form, the one table, post_check_in's reading_confirmed and different_because), and the read-back says "{value}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by you." or "{typed}, typed. {source} said {value}: {reason}." Nothing reads the reason to decide a status, a flag, an attention count or an order: no review flag, no mark against the owner. (Copy.)
- `READING-SEVEN-DAYS`: A reading more than 7 days old (RULES.readingMaxDays, one limit for every metric) is not filled in and its value is not shown anywhere on the step: "{source} last read this on {date}, {n} days ago. That is too old to fill in. Type this week's number, or say there isn't one." with the warning mark, the step's Continue and No new number this week. (Copy.)
- `READING-SHOWN`: Where a check-in's number came from shows beyond the check-in, from what the check-in recorded (Faro keeps no series of readings): the goal's Measured by says "This week's number" from its latest check-in ("{value}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by {name}." or "{typed}, typed by {name}. {source} said {value}.", nothing when it recorded none); each History row says "From {source}, read {when}. {name} checked in." or "Typed by {name}. {source} said {value}. {Reason}: “{words}”"; the metric's page lists its goals with "In its check-in" ("Filled in from {source} · last read {when}", "Typed by hand: {source} has no number per team" or "Typed by hand: no source can be read") and "In the last 8 weeks, {k} of {n} check-ins filled in from {source} used a different number." with See them (goals and weeks, never people); a review's agenda row says "· from {source}" in the quiet ink after a confirmed number, and nothing for a typed one; the Check-ins sheet has Number from, Source's number, Measured at and Reason for a different number, for reading, never loaded back; get_goal and get_metric say the same. (Copy.)

## Help

- **Metrics: what each number means** (`metrics`): The metric library: each number goals are measured by, defined once, with its page saying what it means and every goal measured by it, side by side.
- **Defining a metric well** (`metric-define`): A metric needs three things to be used: a name, a unit and which way is better. The rest can be said later, and its page says what is still to say, in words, never as a score.
- **Measured by: choosing a goal’s metric** (`metric-measured-by`): In New goal and when changing a goal, say which metric measures it by typing to find one, or add one there.
- **Measured by: for whom, and which part** (`metric-slices`): What a goal takes from its metric and what stays its own, whose number it is, and one part of that number.
- **Changing, retiring and merging a metric** (`metric-change`): Which changes save at once, the ones that tell a metric’s goals first, and retiring, bringing back and merging.
- **When a number isn’t measured yet** (`metric-measurement`): Say a metric is measured, partly measured or a gap, and what happens to the goals it measures.
- **Where a metric sits, and how far to trust it** (`metric-structure`): Say what a metric is part of, how much its number can be trusted, and how it could be gamed, so the library keeps a register’s thinking.
- **Draft, Defined and Verified metrics** (`metric-quality`): How far a metric can be trusted: whether its definition is complete, and whether someone other than its owner has reproduced its figure.
- **Metrics in a spreadsheet** (`metric-sheet`): Export the Metrics sheet, change or add rows, and load it back through the same preview, questions and Undo as any import.
